dod_intent_evidence: Two Air Force Direct-to-Phase-II SBIRs, 2023 (~$1.25M each, own abstracts in pack): AI runway FOD detection and AI perimeter security, both piloted at Ellsworth AFB via AFWERX.
score_evidence: "Our team consistently develops integrated AI solutions which provide deployable near real-time better-than-human detection." → lab_language_intensity
"If you can see it, we can solve it" (repeated three times across the site) → lab_language_intensity

"The cameras required for the system will be integrated with vehicles and with pre-existing fixed locations (e.g. light posts, etc.)" — a camera network on an Air Force base, with zero mention of ATO/RMF, STIG, IL levels, or CMMC anywhere in 1,633 words → deployment_awareness_absence

blind_spots.blind_spot: The Ellsworth pilots are an RMF/ATO problem before they are an AI problem, and their language never touches it
blind_spots.operator_reality: Cameras bolted to vehicles and light posts feeding near-real-time alerts means new sensors and compute on an installation network — that requires RMF accreditation, STIGed hosts, and an ISSO-owned package. The 2023 Phase II clock runs out while the accreditation package is being discovered; the algorithm's accuracy never gets a vote.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Commercial anchor is airport/checkpoint screening delivered through OEM partners ('We collaborate directly with our partners' development teams'), so the partner has always owned the accreditation and integration burden.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The cameras required for the system will be integrated with vehicles and with pre-existing fixed locations (e.g. light posts, etc.) and used during runway inspection for FOD.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Near real-time notifications' assumes a delivery path to the Airman that nobody has engineered
blind_spots.operator_reality: How does the alert reach the on-duty Airman — a phone that isn't allowed on the flight line network, a radio call, a base C2 console? Who maintains the vehicle-mounted cameras through a South Dakota winter (lens icing, dust, vibration), and who retrains the model when snow and jackrabbits flood it with false positives? No sustainment, training, or notification-endpoint design appears anywhere in their language.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Solutions are 'actively deployed worldwide' inside partner-run checkpoint hardware in climate-controlled terminals; austere outdoor sustainment has never been their problem.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AAI will develop Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms and a FOD data gathering platform to provide on-duty Airmen with notifications of FOD in near real-time.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A use-case pilot at one base with no named transition sponsor is how D2P2s die
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'AAI will use Ellsworth AFB as a use case' is operator-level advocacy at a single installation. Without a champion above the wing — AFCEC, AFIMSC, or a program office that owns airfield infrastructure — a successful demo ends when the period of performance does; Airmen loving the FOD alerts is not adoption. Months-to-field beyond the funded months is exactly the valley.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: AFWERX D2P2 structure rewards a willing test base, not an acquisition pathway; the team page shows no one with DoD acquisition or program-transition background.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AAI will use Ellsworth AFB as a use case for technology.

opener_hook: Analytical AI's two 2023 AFWERX Phase IIs put cameras on Ellsworth's light posts and patrol vehicles — an installation-network RMF package with no visible ISSO or transition sponsor, and the period of performance is the countdown.
what_they_do: AI threat- and anomaly-detection for imaging (checkpoint/baggage screening commercially; runway FOD and perimeter security for the Air Force).
